meta.question: How does the Department of Commerce select surrogate country datasets for foreign input valuation in trade investigations?

passages.text: In Final Determination A-570-967, the Department rejected a broad 12-country world market average input dataset after respondents demonstrated that only 2 surrogate countries provided tariff classifications specifically disaggregated to the input grade. While narrow 1-3 country selections risk higher price volatility, specificity and comparability took statutory precedence.

The Department of Commerce selects surrogate country datasets based on economic comparability (GNI per capita), production comparability, and data specificity to the investigated merchandise. Under standard practice, broad multi-country baskets may be rejected in favor of narrow sets when broad baskets include distorted prices or non-comparable product classifications.
